editorial:
Imagine being in the room where the biggest decisions of World War II were made. You get to see exactly how Japan decided to enter the war through the eyes of General Hideki Tojo. Beat Takeshi plays the lead role, and he brings a very grounded feel to a man who is usually seen only as a villain in history books. The movie focuses on a tight three month window leading up to the attack on Pearl Harbor, so you spend most of your time watching tense meetings and political fights. It feels more like a high-stakes drama than a typical war movie because the battle is happening in boardrooms and offices rather than on a beach.

What really works here is the acting and the way it shows the pressure these leaders were under. While it can feel a bit slow since there are a lot of people talking in suits, the tension builds up nicely. If you like history, you will love how it breaks down the logic used to justify the war. You should definitely try to find this on a high-quality stream like Prime Video or rent it on Apple TV to catch all the detail. If you are a collector, adding the Blu-ray to your shelf is a great move for a rainy day movie marathon.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up as the plans for the attack on Pearl Harbor are finalized. You see the heavy weight of the decision as Tojo and his team commit to a path they cannot turn back from. It ends with the actual strike on December 7, 1941. The final scenes show that while they achieved a quick victory, they had just started a massive war that would eventually lead to Tojo's own trial and execution.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves history and political dramas.
